module.title: Bacterial Lol-dependent outer-membrane lipoprotein trafficking
module.description: A diderm-bacterial module for delivery of mature lipoproteins from the inner membrane to the outer membrane. The inner-membrane ABC-superfamily complex LolCDE uses ATP hydrolysis by LolD to extract an outer-membrane-destined lipoprotein from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane, without moving it across the bilayer, and hands it to the periplasmic carrier LolA. LolA shields the lipid anchor while crossing the periplasm and passes the lipoprotein mouth-to-mouth to the outer-membrane lipoprotein LolB, which incorporates it into the outer membrane. Lipoproteins with an inner-membrane retention signal are not released. Lipoprotein maturation and the functions of individual lipoproteins lie outside the module. Escherichia coli K-12, in which the pathway was defined, and Pseudomonas putida KT2440 supply exact exemplars for all five components.

evidence.title: lipoprotein localization to outer membrane
evidence.statement: GO:0044874 captures the shared biological-process outcome of the three-stage Lol pathway.

evidence.title: lipoprotein releasing activity
evidence.statement: GO defines this activity for the LolCDE complex of diderm bacteria: recognizing mature outer-membrane lipoproteins in the inner membrane and releasing them for transport across the periplasm.

evidence.title: lipoprotein carrier activity
evidence.statement: GO:0140598 describes binding and carrying a lipoprotein between two cellular locations, the LolA activity.

evidence.title: A new ABC transporter mediating the detachment of lipid-modified proteins from membranes.
evidence.statement: Reconstitution identifies E. coli LolCDE as the ATP-dependent release complex and shows that it does not transport its substrate across the membrane.
evidence.supporting_text: The LolCDE complex differs mechanistically from all other ABC transporters as it is not involved in the transmembrane transport of substrates.

evidence.title: Disruption of lolCDE, encoding an ATP-binding cassette transporter, is lethal for Escherichia coli and prevents release of lipoproteins from the inner membrane.
evidence.statement: LolC, LolD and LolE are each essential, and LolCDE is the sole lipoprotein-release apparatus in E. coli.
evidence.supporting_text: both LolC and LolE were essential for the release of lipoproteins

evidence.title: A novel periplasmic carrier protein involved in the sorting and transport of Escherichia coli lipoproteins destined for the outer membrane.
evidence.statement: Identification of LolA as the periplasmic lipoprotein carrier.
evidence.supporting_text: p20 is a periplasmic carrier protein involved in the translocation of lipoproteins from the inner to the outer membrane

evidence.title: A novel outer membrane lipoprotein, LolB (HemM), involved in the LolA (p20)-dependent localization of lipoproteins to the outer membrane of Escherichia coli.
evidence.statement: LolB is an essential outer-membrane lipoprotein that accepts lipoprotein from LolA and is required for its incorporation.
evidence.supporting_text: When the Lpp-LolA complex was incubated with a water-soluble LolB derivative, Lpp was transferred from LolA to LolB.

evidence.title: Model of mouth-to-mouth transfer of bacterial lipoproteins through inner membrane LolC, periplasmic LolA, and outer membrane LolB.
evidence.statement: Photo-cross-linking supports direct LolC-LolA and LolA-LolB hand-over through the carriers' cavity entrances.
evidence.supporting_text: These results indicate that the transfer of lipoproteins through Lol proteins occurs in a mouth-to-mouth manner.

evidence.title: OpenScientist research for the reusable Lol trafficking module
evidence.statement: The report supports the post-maturation three-stage boundary, confines ATP use to LolCDE extraction, distinguishes mechanotransmission from transmembrane pore transport, and identifies lineage variation in extractor and outer-membrane-delivery architecture.

evidence.title: OpenScientist PSEPK Lol-pathway satisfiability review
evidence.statement: The report independently identifies lolC/PP_2154, lolD/PP_2155, lolE/PP_2156, lolA/PP_4003, and lolB/PP_0724 as the complete canonical KT2440 system and finds no biological gap.

module.notes: Boundary: the module begins with extraction of an already mature outer-membrane-destined lipoprotein and ends with outer-membrane delivery. Lgt/LspA/Lnt maturation is upstream and substrate-specific lipoprotein function is downstream. Generalization: the LolCDE-LolA-LolB relay is conserved beyond Pseudomonas, so the module is species-neutral and uses E. coli K-12 (the organism with the defining biochemistry and genetics) and P. putida KT2440 as exemplars; every leaf grounds to UniProt members of both. The modeled three-part relay is the canonical implementation and not a claim that every diderm lineage has LolB or a heterodimeric LolC/LolE extractor; LolB is mainly found in beta- and gammaproteobacteria, and some lineages encode a single LolC-type membrane subunit. GO terms: LolCDE carries GO:0140306 lipoprotein releasing activity (a protein transporter activity, not a transmembrane transporter activity) and LolA carries GO:0140598 lipoprotein carrier activity; GO has no molecular-function term for the LolB acceptance and insertion step, which the LolB gene reviews record as a proposed new term. Family grounding: PANTHER:PTHR30489 covers both LolC and LolE; its subfamilies do not separate the two roles outside enterobacteria (KT2440 LolC and LolE are both in SF0), so the operon order lolC-lolD-lolE is what assigns the roles. LolB has no PANTHER family assignment in UniProt and is grounded to the NCBIfam LolB family TIGR00548, which both exemplars match. Subunit functions are deliberately asymmetric: the integral subunits LolC and LolE enable GO:0140306 lipoprotein releasing activity (they recognize cargo and recruit LolA), whereas the cytoplasmic ATPase LolD enables GO:0016887 ATP hydrolysis activity and only contributes_to GO:0140306 in its gene reviews.

taxa.description: The canonical LolCDE-LolA-LolB route operates in the diderm envelope; it is best characterized in gammaproteobacteria (E. coli, Pseudomonas).

annotons.role_description: Terminal pathway step that accepts lipoprotein from LolA and incorporates it into the outer membrane. No GO molecular-function term exists for this acceptance and insertion activity, so no function is asserted.

connections.description: LolCDE loads released lipoprotein onto LolA.
LolA presents its lipoprotein cargo to LolB.

knowledge_gaps.gap_statement: Diderm lineages vary between heterodimeric LolC/LolE and homodimeric LolF-type extractors, and some lack a canonical LolB receptor; what replaces LolB in lineages lacking it is not established.
knowledge_gaps.boundary: Treat this document as the canonical LolCDE-LolA-LolB route and model lineage-specific replacements as explicit variants when grounded.

provenance.supporting_text: Whether all diderms use a LolA-type soluble carrier, and what receptor (if any) substitutes for LolB in lineages lacking it, are open.

knowledge_gaps.gap_statement: LolA and LolB are normally required in the canonical relay but can be genetically bypassed under envelope-stress conditions in E. coli; how lipoproteins reach the outer membrane in the bypass state is unknown.
knowledge_gaps.boundary: Do not generalize conditional bypass or essentiality to other organisms without target-organism evidence.

provenance.supporting_text: how substrates reach the outer membrane in the bypass state (diffusion? alternative factors?) is unresolved.

knowledge_gaps.gap_statement: The atomic mechanism of cargo hand-off at the LolCDE-LolA and LolA-LolB interfaces, and of LolB-mediated insertion of the lipid anchor into the outer membrane, is unresolved.
knowledge_gaps.boundary: LolC-LolA docking, LolA-to-LolB transfer and LolB-dependent incorporation are established; the molecular choreography is not.

provenance.supporting_text: The **atomic choreography** of cargo hand-off at each interface, and the physiological route in the LolA/LolB-bypass state, remain unresolved.
